metadata.title: Life Probabilities Deep — Health, Fitness, Relationships, Immigration
metadata.description: Comprehensive probability data for life simulation covering weight loss, fitness, diets, addiction, mental health, relationships, marriage, friendship, and immigration/relocation
sources: CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention)
NIH / NIAAA (National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism)

general_success_rates.source: American Journal of Clinical Nutrition / National Weight Control Registry
general_success_rates.notes: Only 20% of overweight individuals succeed at long-term weight loss (10%+ maintained 1yr)
People regain more than half the weight lost within 2 years

cohabitation_effect.notes: 48% more likely to end vs post-engagement cohabiters

cohabitation_effect.metric: Americans who believe cohabitation improves marriage odds
cohabitation_effect.notes: Evidence does not support this belief

cohabitation_effect.explanation: Couples who cohabit before engagement may marry due to sunk costs (lease, furniture, social pressure) rather than intentional commitment

marriage_satisfaction_over_time.finding: Satisfaction declines within first year of marriage
After 5 years married, satisfaction lower than 6 years before marriage
67.6% of couples show NO significant decline over 20 years
U-shaped curve: decline for first 10 years, then rebound for next 20 years
Couples who stay together: quality does NOT decline on average
Spousal age gap >10 years: faster satisfaction decline
